title: Claude Managed Agents & Dynamic Workflows
content:
## Overview

In 2026, Anthropic expanded the Claude platform with two major agentic capabilities: **Managed Agents** (cloud-hosted agents that run multi-step tasks autonomously) and **Dynamic Workflows** (Claude Code's ability to coordinate hundreds of parallel subagents inside a single session). Together, these represent Anthropic's approach to operating AI at software-engineering scale.

---

## Claude Managed Agents

Managed Agents are AI systems built on Claude that handle full multi-step tasks — planning, execution, and self-correction — without requiring human guidance at every step. They run on Anthropic's cloud infrastructure, not inside a user's session.

### Three New Features (May 2026)

**Dreaming**
A scheduled background process that reviews past agent sessions, surfaces recurring patterns, and curates memory so agents improve between runs. Dreaming happens outside active sessions, letting agents accumulate institutional knowledge without requiring explicit memory management from developers.

**Outcomes**
A framework for tracking whether an agent actually achieved the goal it was given. Rather than logging only tool calls and token usage, Outcomes captures success/failure signals that feed back into Dreaming and help developers identify where agents break down.

**Multiagent Orchestration**
A lead agent breaks a job into parallel pieces and delegates each to a specialist subagent with its own model, prompt, and tool set. Subagents work on a shared filesystem; their outputs flow back into the lead agent's context. Every delegation step is visible in the Claude Console — which agent did what, in what order, and why.

### Availability

Managed Agents are available via the Claude Platform and also via the Claude Platform on AWS (with AWS authentication and billing). Multi-agent orchestration is currently in public beta.

---

## Dynamic Workflows in Claude Code

Dynamic Workflows are Claude Code's answer to codebase-scale engineering tasks. Instead of running one agent per session, Claude dynamically writes orchestration scripts that spawn **tens to hundreds of parallel subagents** in a single session — then validates all outputs before delivering a consolidated result.

### How It Works

1. Claude receives a large task (e.g., migrate a 500K-line codebase from one framework to another)
2. It writes an orchestration script that breaks the work into parallelizable chunks
3. Subagents execute each chunk concurrently on a shared filesystem
4. Claude validates the merged output for consistency and correctness
5. The final, verified result is returned to the user

This pattern allows, for example, codebase-scale migrations from kickoff to merge in a single Claude Code session with Opus 4.8.

### Availability

Dynamic Workflows are available in **research preview** for:
- Claude Code CLI, Desktop app, and VS Code extension (Max, Team, and Enterprise plans with admin enablement)
- Claude API directly
- Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry

---

## Agent View in Claude Code

Alongside Dynamic Workflows, Claude Code added **Agent View** — a unified interface to manage all running Claude Code sessions:
- Start new agents and send them to the background
- Monitor status and last-response summaries without switching contexts
- Jump back into a session only when human input is needed

This complements the Scheduled Tasks feature that lets agents run recurring jobs on Anthropic-managed infrastructure outside of any active session.

---

## Comparison: Managed Agents vs. DIY Orchestration

| | Managed Agents | DIY (API + MCP) |
|---|---|---|
| Infrastructure | Anthropic-hosted | Self-managed |
| Observability | Claude Console with trace | Custom logging |
| Memory | Dreaming (automatic) | Application code |
| Parallelism | Multiagent orchestration | Manual subagent spawning |
| Setup complexity | Low | High |
| Customization | Moderate | Full |

For teams that want rapid deployment with built-in observability, Managed Agents offer significant leverage. For teams with complex custom requirements or existing infrastructure, the API-direct approach remains more flexible.
